mainEntity.name: How long do flexible dentures last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of flexible dentures varies depending on individual factors such as oral hygiene, dietary habits, and changes in the gums and jawbone over time. As a general indication, many patients may expect flexible dentures to last between three and eight years, though this can differ considerably. Our detailed guide on how long flexible dentures last covers the factors that influence lifespan and when replacement may be needed. Over time, the fit may change as the underlying bone naturally resorbs, which may require a reline or replacement. Regular dental check-ups help monitor the condition of your dentures and ensure they continue to fit comfortably and function effectively.

mainEntity.name: Can flexible dentures replace all my teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flexible dentures are primarily designed as partial dentures, meaning they replace some teeth whilst the remaining natural teeth help support the prosthetic. They are generally not recommended as full dentures for patients who have lost all their teeth in an arch. For complete tooth replacement, your dentist may discuss alternative options such as traditional full dentures or implant-supported solutions. The most appropriate treatment depends on your individual clinical circumstances, which can be assessed during a dental consultation.

mainEntity.name: Are flexible dentures better than acrylic dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither option is universally better — each has advantages and limitations that may make it more suitable for certain patients. Flexible dentures tend to be thinner, lighter, and more aesthetically discreet, while acrylic dentures are generally easier to repair and adjust. The most appropriate choice depends on individual clinical factors, which your dentist can assess during a consultation.
